summary: A two-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Noice and Offence, which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Winks did the music and Pal the graphics.
why: Sceners single out the cover of an Amiga Enigma tune, the tribute to the Ocean loader music and the colour cycling. The three-line scroller also gets mentioned, though some find there are too many scrollers.

quote.text: it's the Enigma tune that draws me back to this time and again.

summary: 64ever's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2001. The released version, 1.1, only reached the public in November 2002, and a mini-diskmag notefile comes with it.
why: Sceners praise its story, graphics, music and consistent mood, and several say it deserves a higher place in the CSDb charts than it has.

quote.text: great graphics, great music and great everything but above all it tells a story, that's the coolest thing!

summary: Recycler is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper, which won the ZX Spectrum 640k Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2012.
why: A win in the 640k Spectrum class at Chaos Constructions 2012.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo with a tape-loading title, which won the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009. evilpaul did the code and graphics, 4mat the music.
why: A compo winner made by two people according to the credits. It is also listed as a pack.

summary: Your Song Is Quiet (Part 2) is a ZX Spectrum demo from The Planet of Leather Moomins, Inward and Cyberpunks Unity, which won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2007.
why: Elph handled code, music and direction, ps did the graphics and direction, and Delilah added more graphics.

summary: Cauldron is a C64 demo from The Dreams, Exceed and Resource, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2008. Linus did the music, AmN and Leon the graphics. A bugfixed 101% version followed in 2014.
why: Sceners praise the witch graphics, the 4x4 plasma and light-flare effects and Linus's tune. A few commenters point out that much of the artwork comes from the game Cauldron.

quote.text: It is a nicely designed demo with well done effects, graphics and music.

summary: IO is an MSX demo by Logon System, which won the Other 8-bit Demo compo at Forever 2015. Overflow did the code, CeD the graphics and Aki the music.
why: Nominated for the That's not Possible on this Platform award at The Meteoriks 2016.

summary: (core) is an Atari VCS 4K intro by wAMMA and Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, which placed fifth in Console/Real Wild at Breakpoint 2007. Ilmarque did most of the work, with Viznut's speech synth and scroller code.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007. Tagged as using speech synthesis.

summary: Fairlight's sci-fi C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at Floppy 2005. Hollowman did code and graphics, with music by Jeff and Maktone.
why: Sceners praise its space atmosphere, coherent design and Jeff's soundtrack. The eclipse effect, vector astronaut and robot-head society are often mentioned.

quote.text: Absolutely amazing atmosphere this demo manages to create. Brilliant screenplay, very coherent both graphically and soundwise.

summary: Ghost NOP is an Amstrad CPC demo from Pulpo Corrosivo and Futurs', which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2024. Toms wrote the main code, rexbeng did the graphics and Zik the music.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. The credits include a 3D sprite, coded by OffseT with graphics by Hwikaa.

summary: Wonderball (aka Happy Birthday Diver) is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by introspec and Triebkraft, made as a birthday present. introspec did the code and design, Key-Jee the music.
why: Tagged as a birthday present with randomized visuals, and it needs a Spectrum 128K.

summary: SHAPE's C64 demo, which came fourth in the demo compo at X 2014. GRG did the code and music, Archmage the graphics. The final version adds directory art, a note file and a second disk side of music.
why: Sceners praise the soundtrack, the comic-like graphics and how well sound and visuals fit together. The disco plotter and the 3D VU meter bars are often mentioned.

quote.text: There is just a magic in how Shape combine sound and visuals.

summary: Censor Design's twelfth Wonderland, a C64 demo on an Alice in Wonderland theme that won the C64 demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Magnar did the music.
why: Sceners single out the colour-cycling effects, the chaos zoomer and the flip scroller, and many rate Magnar's soundtrack highly. Some thought the pacing and the sampled sound effects were hit and miss.

quote.text: part after part with amazing effects that most of the time fools you into thinking you're actually watching a really, really good AMIGA demo.

summary: Drunk Chessboard is an Atari 8-bit intro by Infinity, which won the Intro compo at QuaST 1996. The video title calls it a 16k intro. Fox did the code, Qba the graphics and X-Ray the music.
why: A compo winner from the mid-1990s Atari scene, made by a three-person team according to the credits.

summary: XAYAX's Atari VCS demo, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. SvOlli did the code and graphics, Skyrunner the music, with more graphics from Titus, Deft and Veto.
why: Tagged as 32k and as featuring the Amiga ball, the checkered bouncing ball from the Amiga's own 1984 demo, here running on the 2600.

summary: Metamerism is a demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4 by Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights, which won the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012.
why: Mad did the code, Degauss the music and code, and Nero the 2D graphics and colours. It uses Krill's loader.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s third Misery, a demo for the C64 DTV that won the Wild compo at Main 2009. Jammer did the music, with code from Benson, Peiselulli and Streettuff.
why: Sceners call it the most polished DTV demo so far, singling out the fast raycaster with its hidden part, the rotozoomer and the 1280-colour picture. The source was released afterwards.

quote.text: I have no idea how they can get the rotozoomer and wolf3d engine running so fast.

summary: Onescreen Colonies #1 is an Amstrad CPC demo by Vanity, which came fourth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics, with music by Tom&Jerry and Shaft.
why: The music is split between Tom&Jerry and Shaft.

summary: Baltak Rampage is an MSX2 demo by Traktor, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Esau did code, graphics and music, with Bore on code.
why: Five artists share the graphics, and the credits include ASCII graphics by Pumbaa.

summary: A C64 collaboration between Horizon, Instinct, Triad and Focus, which won the demo compo at X 2006 and was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform. Jackasser and Pernod coded it, Linus did the music.
why: Sceners praise its clean design and sense of motion, the giant twister and double zoomscroll, and Linus's tunes. A few find it short or light on effects.

quote.text: A great demo with great sense of motion and great clean design!

summary: Pure is an Atari 8-bit demo by LaResistance, which won the Demo compo at Glucholazy 2008. Pr0be did the code, Born the music and Powrooz the graphics.
why: A compo winner made by a team of three according to the credits.

summary: CRTC³ is an Amstrad CPC demo from Flower Corp., Futurs' and X-Men, which won the Combined Demo compo at Alchimie 2017. The video title calls it a 6128+ cartridge demo.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018. Roudoudou did the code, Hwikaa the graphics and Zik the music and music player.

summary: Tailwind is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gemba Boys, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2016. Aki did the music and some of the graphics, and the tags mark it as AY music.
why: Noby, mborik and Busy share the code, with graphics from mborik, Lamer Pinky and Aki.

summary: Ascend is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Mafia and Cluster, which won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Kylearan did the code and design, KK the music.
why: Tagged as 32k.

summary: SHAPE's full-disk-side C64 demo, the 100% version that completes their Artillery 85% from Little Computer People 2009. GT did the music, Archmage the graphics and 6R6 the main code.
why: Sceners rate GT's tune as one of the best SID soundtracks and admire Archmage's multicolour pictures. Some point out that the pictures had appeared in earlier releases.

quote.text: Great tune Geir, it keeps evolving all the way through and never gets dull.

summary: Ganzfeld is a ZX Spectrum demo by Baze, which came third in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist. The fact sheet has no credits.

summary: Focus's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Big Floppy People 2006. Its design is built around words, with code by Mirage, The Dark Judge and WVL, graphics by Sander and music by Hein.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2006. Sceners praise the minimalistic design, the choreography and Hein's funky tune.

quote.text: A demo that uses minimalistic gfx in a stylish and coherent way.

summary: Reditus is an Atari 8-bit demo by Zelax, which won the Demo compo at QuaST 2004. Święty did the code, Pink the music, with graphics by Dracon and Pazur.
why: A compo winner on the Atari 8-bit, with a four-person credit list.

summary: Eerie Forest is a one-screen intro for the Amstrad Plus/GX4000 by Logon System, based on Shadow of the Beast. It came second in the Combined Demo compo at Alchimie 2017.
why: Overflow did the code and the graphics and music conversions, with extra design and animation by TotO.

summary: SHAPE's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017. Archmage and Carrion did the graphics, with music by Linus and Kristian Røstøen.
why: Sceners single out Archmage's graphics, the stencil effects and the smooth transitions, and several say it should have won. One calls it a prod that blurs the line between demo, slideshow and art.

quote.text: It's one of those prods that erases the lines between demo, slideshow and art.

summary: A two-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Noice and Offence, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Pal did the graphics, and nine coders share the code.
why: Sceners praise the slick transitions, the snake plasma and Pal's graphics. A few feel it leans on scrollers and lacks a bit of heavyweight code.

quote.text: this is pure and unadulterated transition heaven.

summary: Triad's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Dane did the music, and the demo loops endlessly.
why: Sceners single out the fisheye terrain view, the greetings upscroller and the dancing martial artist at the end, set to Dane's music. The usual complaint is that it is short.

quote.text: I love the narrativity and the flow. Great effects and overall feeling.

summary: C-Drug is an Atari 8-bit demo from Agenda, Mad Team and LaResistance, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11. The video title calls it an Atari 130XE demo.
why: Probe and Tebe share the code, stRing did the music, and Ooz and Ripek the graphics.

summary: Plush's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. Krill wrote the code, Fanta, Gangstar and Dgazz did the music. It is tagged as German-language and humorous.
why: Sceners praise how well the parts are linked and its distinctive style, and several name it their favourite C64 demo. Many are surprised it dates from 2000.

quote.text: each time i dig it out of my diskbox i think of the transitions between parts in this demo.

summary: Black Mail's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at the Silicon Limited Winter Party 1991. Hein did the graphics, Jeroen Tel and Reyn Ouwehand the music.
why: Sceners credit it with a turning point in C64 demo design, and praise the pixel art, the soundtrack and the flow. Its joyport interaction and Mix-e-load loader are often recalled. Voted joint 18th best in Design #1.

quote.text: it created a turning point in design and style in the world of C64 demos.

summary: Breaking Baud is an Amstrad CPC demo by CRTC, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Doz and MaV did the code and McKlain the music.
why: Graphics are by Jeni, rexbeng and Tunk (font), and the source is available.

summary: A Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with code and graphics by Snorpung and music by Nordloef. The video was captured on a real Game Boy Color.
why: Tagged as 1mbit and set to loop endlessly.

summary: OMD - Orb MegaDemo is a VIC-20 demo by Orb, which came second in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. Ultra and 4-Mat did the code, with 4-Mat on music.
why: Keops made the loading screen. A podium finish on the VIC-20.

summary: Censor Design's three-disk-side C64 demo, the thirteenth Wonderland, which came third in the demo compo at X 2016. It carries an Alice in Wonderland theme and dance animations.
why: It won That's Not Possible On This Platform at The Meteoriks 2017. Sceners single out the sampled Prodigy finale, the bob snakes and Joe's pixel art; some find the design less finished than usual for Censor.

quote.text: Rock solid demo, with a good pace, cleverly built layered routines, and an ace digi that has some of the cleanest bass drums I have ever heard on a C64.

summary: New View 48K is a ZX Spectrum demo by Conscience, which came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2015. Alone Coder led the code, with music by nq.
why: Nominated for the That's not Possible on this Platform award at The Meteoriks 2016. Tagged as a sprites record and as using multicolour mode on a 48K Spectrum with AY sound.

summary: Fairlight's 1970s disco-themed C64 demo, the 75% party version, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2005 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2005.
why: Sceners praise the design, the colour use and Reed's disco soundtrack, though some argue it does not feel much like the 1970s. Abaddon points to the improved version 1.1 as the one to watch.

quote.text: The programming is cool, but the design is the thing that stands out.

summary: Phortem is an Amstrad CPC demo by Condense, listed for both the CPC and the Amstrad Plus. The video shows the Amstrad Plus version.
why: No Recess did the code, CeD the graphics, Dma-Sc the music and Arnoldemu the disc loader.

summary: Notizen aus der Provinz is a C16/Plus 4 demo by The Electronic Knights, which won the Combined 8bit Demo/Intro compo at SceneCon 2007. Degauss did the code, graphics and music, with graphics from Luca.
why: A win in a combined 8-bit demo and intro compo.

summary: DTC is an Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders and Arkos. Ramlaid did the code, Beb the graphics and design, and Jedi the music.
why: The end part uses music by David Whittaker.

summary: Goa is a ZX Spectrum 128K 4K intro by Extreme Entertainment, which won the 4K Intro compo at Funtop 1998. Exploder did the code.
why: The source is available, and it was ported to the ZX Next in 2026.

summary: Where Have All The Pixels Gone? is a Vectrex demo by the Carnegie Mellon University Computer Club, which won the Combined Demo compo at Pixel Jam 2012. It is also listed as an invitation.
why: Tagged as featuring Nyan Cat. Eight people share the code, graphics and music credits.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, which won the demo compo at X 2024 and Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2025. Trident wrote the code, The Sarge and Soya did the graphics, Fegolhuzz and Danko the music.
why: Sceners praise the story and direction, the pace and the new effects such as the zooming bobs and FLESCOS. Many say it makes a strong case for concept demos on the C64.

quote.text: A supremely entertaining demo with a breathless, exhilarating pace.

summary: Triad's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013. Dane did the music and Twoflower the graphics, including the fullscreen picture St. Joaquin.
why: Sceners praise the smooth transitions between the work of many coders, the design and the soundtrack. Some feel the killer effects are missing, and a few note echoes of Edge of Disgrace.

quote.text: Twoflower's graphics are wonderful, Danes music fits perfectly and the code masters do a brilliant job to create a coherent, flowing, smooth as silk prod.

summary: Add Mortem is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Arise and Joker, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at speccy.pl party 2025. Jammer did the music, with code from Luke, Wacek and Dalthon.
why: It won Best Demo at the GOTY ZX Spectrum Awards 2025 and Best Soundtrack at The Meteoriks 2026, where it was also nominated for Best Oldschool Production.

summary: Prosonix and Offence's comeback C64 demo, a press-space megademo that won the C64 demo compo at X 2010. It is dedicated to the memory of Unitrax and uses Iron Maiden and joker themes.
why: Sceners praise its spirit, graphics and music, and the interweaving scrollers and isometric DYCP. Some find it uneven or dislike the press-space format. It was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

quote.text: this one oozes the right spirit and creativity I like.
